messages:
sarah: Quick q — if we need to emergency-disable model-serving v2, who is authorized to flip the hot-stop? I want to update the runbook before EOD.

alex: Oncall has immediate authority for prod emergencies. If it's a safety/reg compliance issue, escalate to an SRE lead first (jamie or priya). For anything else, oncall can flip.

jamie: +1. Also: we should record reason + incident id when flipping. Runbook currently says "oncall", but doesn't list audit steps — we need to add the exact command and where logs go.

mike: Where do the audit logs surface? Is it CloudTrail / ops-audit S3 or centralized DB?

alex: ops-audit S3 bucket + we push an entry to the incident tracker (we have a small lambda that writes to /ops/events). Example command (internal utility):

```
opsctl feature toggle disable model-serving-v2 --scope=prod --by=oncall --reason="safety:excessive-errors" --incident=INC-3421
```

jamie: Perfect. Add also a tag for "canary-only" if you're doing a limited rollback: `--scope=prod:canary` will only stop the canary layer.

oncall-bot: ACTION LOGGED: `opsctl` run by @alex. Logged to ops-audit (s3://redwood-ops-audit/2023/11/10/opsctl.log). If this was a test, run `opsctl feature toggle rollback ...` to re-enable.

sarah: Who can override an oncall flip? For example, if oncall accidentally disables the whole fleet and we need to re-enable.

jamie: Only SRE leads and product owners can force an override after review. We need a 2nd-party approval for global re-enables in production. Add note: emergency re-enables must include postmortem link.

ops-bot: Created ticket INC-3421 in PagerDuty -> Jira bridge. Owner: @sarah. Audit ID: audit_20231110_65b2

mike: Small edge-case: private deployment customers — oncall can't flip those remotely unless they gave us delegated access. Add a line in runbook to confirm scope before pressing the button.

sarah: Great. I'll PR the runbook changes: add `opsctl` examples, audit bucket path, who can override, and canary flags. Ping me for review @jamie @alex :thumbsup:

alex: thanks — lgtm once PR has the exact commands and the policy bit.

jamie: I'll add a short test scenario for the weekly oncall drill so everyone practices the flow.

sarah: awesome, filing now. Link to current runbook for context: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/hotstop-and-emergency-toggle>
